subject: Urban Planning
title: Le Corbusier's Plan Voisin: The City That Wasn't Built
description: Learn Le Corbusier's Plan Voisin: The City That Wasn't Built in one minute.

hook.text: In 1925, Le Corbusier proposed demolishing central Paris and replacing it with 60-story cruciform towers.

buildup.text: Plan Voisin would have erased the Marais district. Streets would become highways. People would live in identical towers.

discovery.text: He saw old neighborhoods as disease-ridden chaos. His solution: light, air, and geometric perfection.

twist.text: Paris rejected it. But Brasília, Chandigarh, and Soviet housing blocks all followed his principles exactly.

climax.text: The towers-in-a-park model failed almost everywhere. People need streets, shops, and messy vitality.

punchline.text: He wanted to demolish Paris. Paris said no. Others said yes — and regretted it.

quiz.question: What did Le Corbusier's Plan Voisin propose for Paris?
options: Building a network of underground highways beneath the city
Demolishing central Paris and replacing it with high-rise towers
Creating a ring of new satellite cities around the existing center
